_comment: Escrito à mão, não gerado. maint/build_adapter_errors.php lê este
arquivo e o mistura ao que baixa das fontes, então regenerar nunca
'families' casa pelo primeiro número do código; 'codes' casa o código
inteiro e ganha da família. O texto é explicação, não tradução: a
mensagem japonesa continua no dado, para quem quiser comparar com a
tela, mas quem chega aqui quer saber o que fazer.

00.title: The game could not reach REON
00.means: A catch-all the game falls back to when it has no better code. In practice it means the same as 10-XXX: the conversation with the adapter never got anywhere.

10.title: The adapter is not there
10.means: The game looked for a Mobile Adapter and found nothing. On an emulator that usually means the adapter is not switched on in the emulator; on real hardware, that the cable or the adapter is not seated.
10.todo: Plug the adapter in before starting the game and leave it in. In mGBA, open Mobile Game Boy Adapter… and make sure it is enabled.

11.title: The call did not go through
11.means: The adapter tried to dial and got nowhere. On REON there is no telephone line — this is the adapter failing to open a connection to the server.
11.todo: Check the machine is online. If you are on real hardware, check the Wi-Fi settings you flashed. Then try again: the game treats this as temporary and so should you.

12.title: The line is busy
12.means: Same family as 11: the adapter could not complete the connection, and the game blames a congested line.
12.todo: Wait a moment and try again.

13.title: The call did not go through
13.means: Another of the dialling failures, shown with the same message as 11-000.
13.todo: Wait a moment and try again; if it never works, check the network side.

14.title: The adapter's settings are damaged
14.means: The configuration stored in the adapter did not pass its own checksum, so the adapter refuses to use it.
14.todo: Load your mobile_config.bin again. It is on Your Account, and the guide says where to put it.

15.title: The adapter got an answer it did not understand
15.means: Something replied, but not in the shape the adapter expected. It is the code REON's own scripts produce when the adapter could not reach a server properly.
15.todo: Try again. If it persists, it is worth reporting — this one usually means the two sides disagree about something, not that you did anything wrong.

16.title: Communication error
16.means: One of the generic failures. The game has no detail to offer beyond "it did not work".
16.todo: Wait and try again. If it repeats in the same place every time, report it with what you were doing.

20.title: The wrong mobile centre was selected
20.means: The adapter tried to reach a service it is not configured for.
20.todo: Load your mobile_config.bin again — it is what points the adapter at REON.

24.title: The connection was refused
24.means: The adapter reached the network but could not open the connection — a TCP failure.
24.todo: Check that nothing on your machine blocks the outgoing connection, then try again.

25.title: The adapter was never set up
25.means: There is no configuration in the adapter at all, so it has nothing to dial.
25.todo: Load your mobile_config.bin, or run the Mobile Trainer to register the adapter.

30.title: The mail server refused the message
30.means: This family is about sending mail. The last three digits are the mail server's own SMTP reply — 4xx is temporary, 5xx is permanent.
30.todo: See the specific code. A 4xx is worth retrying; a 5xx will keep failing until something changes.

31.title: The mailbox server returned an error
31.means: This family is about collecting mail over POP3.
31.todo: Try again. If it repeats, your account may need attention — check you can read the same mailbox from REON Mail.

32.title: The web request failed
32.means: This family is about the HTTP requests a game makes for rankings, news and downloads. The last three digits are the HTTP status the server replied with.

33.title: The mobile centre reported a problem
33.means: The service answered, but with a complaint of its own rather than the data the game asked for.
33.todo: Wait and try again. If one particular feature always fails this way, report it — it points at that feature, not at your setup.

101.title: The connection broke underneath
101.means: A socket-level failure: the connection dropped, timed out or was reset while the game was using it.
101.todo: These are usually the network, not the game. Try again on a steadier connection.

30-221.means: The mail server closed the conversation. Often harmless on its own.

30-421.means: The mail server is not accepting mail right now (SMTP 421). Temporary.

30-450.means: The mailbox was unavailable (SMTP 450). Temporary — try later.

30-451.means: The server hit an error of its own while handling the message (SMTP 451). Temporary.

30-452.means: The server is out of room (SMTP 452). Temporary.

30-550.means: There is no such mailbox (SMTP 550). Check the address you typed in the game.

30-551.means: The address is not local to that server (SMTP 551).

30-552.means: The message is too large for the mailbox (SMTP 552).

30-553.means: The address is not a valid one (SMTP 553). Check what you typed.

30-554.means: The server refused the message outright (SMTP 554).

31-002.means: The POP3 server answered with an error. On REON this is usually a login the server did not accept.

32-301.means: The page moved (HTTP 301). The game does not follow redirects, so this fails.

32-302.means: The page moved temporarily (HTTP 302). Same problem: the game does not follow it.

32-401.means: The server wanted credentials the game did not send (HTTP 401).

32-404.means: The server has nothing at that address (HTTP 404). On REON this usually means a game or a feature we do not serve yet.

32-500.means: Something broke on our side (HTTP 500). Worth reporting with the time it happened.

32-502.means: A bad answer came back through the front door (HTTP 502). Usually brief.

32-503.means: The service is down or overloaded (HTTP 503). Try later.

32-504.means: Our side took too long to answer (HTTP 504). Try later.
